newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end weak, little fund action seen.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end weak, little fund action seen.

text.p: ** (1010 GMT) Bombay shares stay in range-bound trade,
maintain morning weakness on little fund buying
** Traders await decision of market regulator later on
Wednesday to consider simplified carry forward trade
** Bombay's benchmark index ends 35.33 pts, or 0.94 pct,
lower at a provisional 3,730.25
** Local markets unaffected by the Federal Reserve's
widely anticipated decision to raise U.S. interest rates
** National exchange index up 1.20 pts, or 0.11 pct, to
1,059.55 on first day of weekly trade account
Shares at Bombay exchanges finished mostly lower on Wednesday and brokers termed the market weakness as a speculator sell-off amid little buying activity by foreign funds.
"It's been pretty confusing. Basically, the markets have been local-operator driven," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking. "There has been little overseas buying."
An overnight quarter percentage point hike in U.S. interest rates by the Federal Reserve was mostly ignored by the local markets, traders said.
"If the increase was larger, a sell-off in U.S. markets could have had a spill-over effect on Indian bourses," said Ramesh Damani, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
Wall Street had turned lower on Tuesday following the Fed's announcement, and ended off 29 points, or 0.4 percent, at 6,876 after a powerful 100-point rally on Monday.

Local markets could attract increased fund buying after a $526.5 million long-awaited Global Depositary Issue (GDR) by Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd was oversubscribed about 10 times, traders said. The firm on Monday said its GDR issue had been priced at $13.93 per GDR, or 1,000 rupees per VSNL share.
Shares of VSNL rose 30 rupees to 1,100 rupees at the BSE. The stock gained 69 rupees, or seven percent, to 1,054.25 at the start of a weekly trade account at the National Stock Exchange.

"The market outlook is quite good, but funds are looking for some price consolidation at current levels," said an equities dealer at a foreign brokerage. "Any volatility puts them off from making fresh commitments in a big way."

Dealers said market focus was also on a board meeting in New Delhi later on Wednesday by market regulator, the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to discuss a simplified carry forward trading system.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
